utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, could you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you and good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-03-67-T, the Prosecutor versus Vojislav Seselj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Registrar. This is Tuesday, October 7, 2008, and I would like to greet the representatives of the OTP, Mr. Seselj, as well as everyone helping us. A witness is scheduled. Are there any protective measures that have been requested?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. No protective measures. That's good news. Let's bring the witness into the courtroom. Mr. Ferrara, how long have you scheduled for this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Three hours, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Three hours. Excellent. Let's bring the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning. Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please tell us your name, surname, and date of birth.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters note, we cannot hear the witness from the background noise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Do you have a job at the moment? If so, what job?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At present, I'm a farmer at a farm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Have you already testified in a court regarding what happened in former Yugoslavia, or is this the first time that you are testifying.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is my first time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Could you please read the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. You may sit down. Before giving the floor to Mr. Ferrara, who is going to examine you, I have a few details to tell you, and I also have a few questions to ask. This is the information I would like to convey to you: You are a Prosecution witness. You've been called by the Prosecution. You have now made the solemn declaration, and you are now a witness of justice. Everything you are saying is under oath. The procedure here is a bit specific. You might not really be very familiar with it. You are supposed to answer questions that will be put to you by the Prosecutor, on your right, and this should take about three hours altogether. The Prosecutor will put questions to you and present you with a number of documents. After this very important phase, the Prosecution phase, we will move on to the second phase, because the accused, Mr. Seselj, who's on your left, can cross-examine you for exactly the same amount of time. His questions will have two purposes; your credibility as a witness as well as the content of the answers you gave. The three Judges on the bench in front of you might also ask questions to you at any moment, notably regarding documents that will be submitted to you. We will have 20-minute breaks every hour and 15 minutes, but if at one point in time you don't feel very well, feel uneasy, would like a break, just ask for it, raise your arm and ask for it. You are under oath, as I told you, which means that now you are no longer supposed to be in contact with the Prosecutor. When tonight you come back to your hotel room, you are not supposed to contact the Prosecution. I have a couple of questions for you, very briefly. Before coming here, were you contacted by the Defence of Mr. Seselj? Did you have any contacts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's how they introduced themselves, actually.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you briefly tell us what happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the first contact was over the telephone, through the chairman of the basic cell of the Radical Party, Mr. Zeljko Dosen, who asked me whether I wanted to have contact with them or, rather, the Defence lawyers wanted to contact me, and I said that they were free to come. After that, they did come, and a certain Mr. Sarovic, who I met for the first time then, had a few questions in relation to what I knew concerning my testimony. My brief answer was that I made a statement to the Prosecution and that I would repeat that in court, and that I didn't wish to discuss it with him. And that's how the matter ended.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This conversation, was it cordial or was it a bit tense?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, one could say that it was normal. I wasn't too excited. There weren't any pressures exerted against me, or any threats, or anything of the kind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. After you said --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I beg your pardon. I would like to add one more thing. There was a proposal from their side as to whether I wished to make a deposition in court for Mr. Seselj's Defence. My brief answer to that was, "No."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] After you told them that you no longer wanted -- that you did not want to testify on their behalf because you were a Prosecution witness, did you get new phone calls telling you that you should change your mind, or did everything stop?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There were other telephone contacts. Dosen and Mr. Sarovic called me in relation to the proposal made, since local elections were being repeated, they suggested to me that I be a candidate for a municipal assemblyman and to join the party. I refused that. There were no other contacts or suggestions made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I beg your pardon. The only thing is that when I arrived here, I was informed by my daughter that Mr. Dosen had phoned and asked about me, which upset me further and caused concern.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your daughter told you that Mr. Dosen had phoned, but Mr. Dosen is a member of the Serbian Radical Party in your municipality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He is the president of the local committee in Hrtkovci.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At any point in time, was your daughter offered a job?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, in the first contacts made by Dosen, he said that they could help me in that way, that they could even give my daughter a job perhaps, and proposals like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but your -- did your daughter get job offers; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know about that. Probably the answer is "no," since she did not tell me about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for answering these few questions regarding the conditions prevailing and which -- and the conditions which made it possible for you to come here to freely testify for the Prosecution. Mr. Ferrara, you now have the floor and you may put all your questions to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Mr. Ejic, just in relation to these last questions, were you ever threatened or approached regarding your decision to be a Prosecution witness from people of your village?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: Yes, but I don't know their names. I know their faces by sight. I was stopped twice, once in the main street and the other time in a small back street when I was on my bicycle. The question was, "Ejic, stop. Could I ask you something? Is it true that you are a Prosecution witness against Seselj?" I smiled and briefly said, "No," and went on on my bike. That first time, there was no other reaction or threat. The second time, though, it was in a back street. Then even a threat was issued against me in the following vein: "Be careful. Think of where you're supposed to go back." I did not engage in dialogue. I continued on bicycle. I went where I wanted to go, and there were no other threats against me.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Were you ever accused that you got some money from the Prosecution to be a Prosecution witness?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: Well, not exactly accused. A friend of mine from way back, Pero Mandic from my street, said to me once in the street -- or, rather, asked me the following: "People are talking around the village that you are a Prosecution witness and that you received 5.000 Euro in order to testify." And my answer to him was, "I don't even want to discuss the trip without 50.000 Euro." So that is how I stopped this conversation with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Was your answer sarcastic?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: Well, precisely, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Did you receive any money from the Prosecution to come and testify?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Was any member of your family ever approached regarding your testimony here?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Was any relative, any member of your family, ever contacted by somebody regarding your decision to come to testify before this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: No, no, I was the only person contacted. However, once my daughter happened to be with me when I had this contact once at the office in Belgrade with the representatives of the OTP.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Let's move to that. Your Honours, I think we should redact this part of the testimony regarding his contact with the Radicals and this approach.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm opposed to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judge Harhoff asked a question first, so I believe he should be answered first and then Mr. Seselj will have the floor. Mr. Ferrara, my colleague just asked you why we should redact.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think that there is the -- still pending the motion regarding the conduct of the associates of the accused with our witness, is the reason.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, there is no rule saying that one of the parties is forbidden from contacting the witnesses of the other party. The Prosecution has just responded to my motion to protect Defence witnesses, that they have the right to have contacts, and they invoked Judge Schomberg's statement from another case, and in this way they invoke case law. Secondly, none of my associates threatened this witness, and the witness never accused any one of my associates. Thirdly, when the witness refused to cooperate with Nemanja Sarovic, Nemanja Sarovic never appeared to see the witness again. Fourthly, the offer made to him by Mr. Dosen to be a candidate in the local elections, that's their very own affair, it's their own village affair. It's a small village and everybody knows each other, and they are having extraordinary elections now for the municipality of Ruma. This witness is a member of a party which, in a way, was an ally of the Serb Radical Party in the post-election negotiations after the Republican elections held in May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, I wanted to ask the witness exactly the same thing, and then I thought that's not really worth it, but now I would like to ask a question after all. Witness, please, earlier you told us that you had been offered to be a candidate for local elections for the Serbian Radical Party, and you declined, and I wondered why. Is it because you're a member of another party? And Mr. Seselj just said that you are a member of another party. Could you tell us whether it's true or not, and if you are a member of another party, which party?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is correct. I'm a member of that party. However --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Why didn't you say so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, no one asked me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wanted to put the question to you, but tell us, okay, which party do you belong to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The party of the New Serbia, Nova Serbia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you tell us who the leader of this party is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Velimir Ilic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe I understood that there are going to be extraordinary elections, and you are going to be on the list of that party.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Elections are about to be held, but I wasn't a candidate at the previous elections, the regular ones. These are extraordinary ones at the Ruma municipality. Now I'm not a candidate now either because I am not involved in that kind of thing anymore, but I did become a member last year, and that's the way things stand now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I must confess that I'm not really very familiar with the political situation in Ruma and around Ruma, but could you please tell us whether your party, the party you belong to, New Serbia, is it a party that is in opposition to the Serbian Radical Party at the moment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it's not in opposition to the Serb Radical Party because at present, well, there was this combination that they would form a coalition in Belgrade, but in Ruma, as far as I know, there is a coalition between the Democratic Party of Serbia and the Party of the New Serbia. That's the coalition that is running in the election. That is to say that these two parties are not in coalition with the Serbian Radical Party.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. This fully answered my question, and I am now enlightened on the political situation in Ruma. Mr. Seselj, please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I'm saying this only by way of argument in order to oppose redactions in the stenographic notes. There is nothing that should remain secret, that should be concealed from the public. After the elections in the month of May, the Serbian Radical Party and the coalition that this witness belonged to, the coalition between Kostunica and Ilic, or rather the Democratic Party of Serbia and New Serbia, concluded an agreement to establish a government in Serbia. This agreement was concluded with the Socialist Party of Serbia. However, they betrayed us then and joined the other camp. That's why that government was not formed. With the Democratic Party of Serbia and the New Serbia of Velimir Ilic, we have agreed to establish local government wherever possible in Serbia. During the previous mandate, the Serbian Radical Party was in power in Ruma. Now it was impossible to establish a new government after the previous elections, so the elections are being repeated and at this local level, we are simply seeking allies to win power again. That is the core of the matter. There is absolutely no reason to redact the transcript whatsoever. I'm explaining that to you. I'm presenting arguments for that. I did not want to delve into the political situation now. What the Prosecution is asking for doesn't make sense at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The Trial Chamber will deliberate on this immediately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] After a lengthy deliberation, Judges believe that there is no need to redact anything. Mr. Ferrara, you may continue your examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Mr. Ejic, can you describe your education for the Chamber?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: I am an agricultural technician in the field of crop production. I have a secondary education.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Are you married?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I am married. I have two children, a son and a daughter, and three grandchildren.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Where did you live in 1992?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: Where I was born, in Hrtkovci, the street of Ive Lole Ribara, number 46. I live there to this day.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: What was the ethnic makeup of the village until the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute. Witness, you gave us the name of your street where you lived. Do you believe that this could stay in the transcript, or would you rather this address not be made public? It is as you like.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, when I first had contacts, I decided to be a protected witness. However, after having realised that half of my town, and even more than that, knew that I would be a witness, I decided to change that and to testify in public. If I had the courage that was required in situations that were far more difficult to go out public and make statements to the media at home and abroad, I think it is right to speak up now as well so that the broader-world public would find out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Ferrara, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Mr. Ejic, what was the ethnic makeup of the village before the start of the war?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: Prior to the falling apart of the former Yugoslavia, to my knowledge, the ethnic composition was as follows: Between 50 and 60 per cent were of Croat ethnicity; some 30-something per cent were Hungarians, and the remaining 10 or so were Serbs or, rather, Orthodox residents, including the Romas.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Can you shortly describe for us the relationships between the different groups before the start of the war?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: The relationships in our town were such that one didn't feel this ethnic diversity. There were many mixed marriages. I am in one such marriage. I'm a Serb -- or, rather, there were marriages where Serbs were married to Croats or Hungarians and so on. There were some individual incidents and cases of excessive behaviour where people expressed ethnic hatred or intolerance, but only at the time when Yugoslavia started falling apart and a multiparty system was introduced. Prior to that, there were no such cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: I forgot to ask you. What's your ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: I'm a Serb by ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Did this relationship change, and what would you describe the reason for this change, if any?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: These relations changed after Yugoslavia fell apart, especially after the first wave of refugees arrived from Croatia and other areas of the former Yugoslavia. Initially, when the multiparty system was introduced, when various political parties were set up, I was one of the founders of a party called the Serbian Renewal Movement. There were many other parties that were founded at the time; for example, the Party of Croats and Hungarians in Vojvodina, then the Serbian Radical Party, then the League of Social Democrats of Vojvodina, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: When? When was this period of time when you say this change, when you say the first -- let's see what you say exactly, when the first wave of refugees arrived from Croatia? Can you give us a date -- a period of time, not a date exactly?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment, Mr. Ferrara. Before the witness answers, I'd like to get back to what you said. From what I understood, you were one of the founders of the Serbian Renewal Movement. You founded this party in your settlement. What I'm interested in is this: Why did you found this party and what was the purpose of it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Initially -- or, rather, before I was an activist of the League of Communists of Yugoslavia. Most people were, because we had a single-party system, and being a member of that party was one of the conditions for finding employment, including myself as well. That was one of the factors that helped me find a job. Now, as for my motives to found the Serbian Renewal Movement with some six to seven other members was that I liked their programme, I liked their platform, and the leader of that party, who remains leader to this day, Vuk Draskovic, I liked his attitude, I liked his appearances and his ideas. He did not express any chauvinism. He only ethnic affiliation and nurturing of Serbian traditions through the party. So those were my motives.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. You've answered my question. I'm satisfied with it. Mr. Ferrara, I apologise for having interrupted you. You may put your question again.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: So when -- can you give us exactly a date or a period of time when there was this change in your village in the relationship between the different ethnic groups. You say when the first wave of refugees arrived. When did it happen?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: That was, I think, in 1991, and more pronounced in 1992. I don't know the exact date, but it was in springtime.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Did you have any political function at the time?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: Yes. At the time, I was the president of the local board. The previous president, Ostoja Sibincic, had resigned after the first refugees arrived, and he mostly focused on contacts with the refugees, providing assistance to them and being involved with them. So he resigned. He also said that he simply became afraid after the Party of Croats and Hungarians was established and decided it was better for him not to be president any longer. So it was his personal choice. At that time, at the session of the local board, the local commune, I was elected president, and I remained president throughout the entire time until the board was dissolved. I can tell you more about that later, if you wish.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Why the board was dissolved?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: My decision for the board to dissolve was grounded on the fact that in the town there were rumours that the SPO party -- or, rather, the Serbian Renewal Movement Party was assisting refugees and their violent behavior and that it was directing them to act that way, which naturally wasn't true. I wrote a communique, and I put it on the board, informing the residents that it wasn't true and that the local board would be dissolved. I also informed the Municipal Board, who supported me in that decision. Later on, I was told that Ostoja Sibincic was banned from the party due to everything that he had done at the time. He was expelled from the party. That was my motive to close down the local board.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: What did Ostoja Sibincic do?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: According to what I know, initially he provided assistance, at the time when the war had just broken out in Croatia, assistance in gathering and sending food and other aid. We had a campaign and organised all that on one occasion. There was a truck driven by Mica Trajakovic, who now resides in the United States, and Mica Trajakovic drove the aid we collected in the truck. However, it didn't end there. He also had other motives; namely, to instigate them to act violently and to threaten in order to pressure local Croats or, rather, local Catholic residents to exchange their homes with the Serbs who had come from other republics such as Croatia or Bosnia. This was the conviction that I held at the time, that was my belief, and I was able to verify it on various occasions, at various gatherings of citizens and based on other sources. I was able to confirm that. I think that it was mostly with the assistance of the regime of Slobodan Milosevic or, rather, the assistance of the Socialist Party that he was able to implement that. Later on, in cooperation with the representatives of the Serbian Radical Party, that mostly consisted of refugees that had arrived, he also continued his work through them. Initially, there were also some local residents involved when the party was set up and their board.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: When did this campaign start?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: Well, this campaign started back in the spring, and it was continued intensely in 1992 and all the way up until his arrest, when he was put in detention due to accusations for these events and some other matters. That is to say, from April until August or September - I'm not sure exactly when he was arrested - of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: When was the Serbian Radical Board -- Serbian Radical Party board in Hrtkovski created?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: I think it was in the spring of 1992, because local elections were held at the time, as well as federal elections. I think that it was during that period of time. One of the local residents, Slobodan Momic, who initially held the post very briefly in that board, he was the one who told us that.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: This Slobodan Momic was the president of the board?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: He wasn't the president. He was a member. According to what I know, the president was a man called Dudic at the time. I can't remember his first name right now. I think it's Blagoje, yes, it's Blagoje Dudic. He's a refugee from Croatia. He exchanged his home at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Do you remember if there was a time when the number of members of the SRS in Hrtkovci increased?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: I think that the number of members increased after the party rally that was held, when Dr. Vojislav Seselj came to our town on the 6th of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I have a short question for you. Mr. Blagoje Dudic was someone you knew well? He lived in the same village as you did, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He does reside there now, but that wasn't the case all the time. I think that he arrived in 1992, when he exchanged his house. And I know him. We're not really close, we just know each other, we're acquaintances. He's in commerce, and I sold my products to him and he resold them further on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I shall rephrase my question and talk about Slobodan Momic. He's someone you know well, isn't he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I know him well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So he tells you that the Serbian Radical Party will be established in your village. Does he give you any reasons why this party should be founded? What is the purpose of this? Why should this party be founded, according to what you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He didn't tell me when he had joined the party. It's just that I learned about that later, when he left the party. His explanation was that the programme of the Serbian Radical Party was initially acceptable to him. And later on, when bad things started happening in our village, he left the party, and he was one of the participants -- he was one of the local residents who went to Belgrade to the Federal Secretariat of the Interior to complain about the situation on our village. On one occasion, he and I appeared on a radio show at the M Radio Station in Sremska Mitrovica where we talked about the problems in Hrtkovci.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My last question. I followed your answers closely. I understood that you were the president of the Municipal Board at one stage, and through your answers, I gather that you know a lot about the political life there. And you told us a while ago that you gave interviews to the foreign press. What I'm interested in is this: I'd like to know, in 1992, when the Serbian Radical Party was founded, what difference was there between those people that join that party and someone like you? At the time, was there a difference between the two or not? Some just joined the one party and other people joined another?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, initially, according to what I know from Momic himself was that he was motivated by the programme. He liked the programme. And later on, he saw that programme was one thing and the events on the ground are quite a different matter, and he left the party.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We might be able to understand things better later. Mr. Ferrara.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Mr. Ejic, you say that when the war was spreading in Croatia, you experienced a change in Hrtkovci in respect to refugees that came to your village. How many refugees would you estimate arrived at your village at the time?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly what the figure was. Initially, perhaps 100 to 200 people, and then at one point in time the situation was such that there were almost as many refugees as residents, or approximately as many, over 1.000 of refugees who had come from Croatia and Bosnia and Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Where did they stay?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: Initially, the first refugees were housed at the Polet agricultural property, where they had accommodation for seasonal workers, and that's where they were housed. And then some individuals were housed in individual homes. Later on, they started entering houses of residents who were absent, whose houses were vacant because the owners lived abroad. There were cases of violent entry and occupation of those houses. That was the situation. There were also many cases where residents were evicted from their own homes. And then after police intervened, they would be allowed back into their own homes, but there were cases of intimidation, threats, even physical violence, and residents were afraid.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: When did this start, these illegal activities?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: These illegal activities became especially prominent after the pre-election rally of the Serbian Radical Party was held.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment. Witness, for the time being, things are moving on very quickly. I'd like to get back and go back in time a little bit before we discuss those illegal activities. We learned from you that a lot of Serbian refugees come to your village, and at some point you say that there were a thousand refugees and they were greater in number than the local residents. If I understand correctly, during that time you held a position in the municipality, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're quite right, if you're referring to -- initially, we, at our own initiative and based on the proposal of the council of the local commune, whose representative was Dobrosav Markovic at the time, we set up a board with constant duty shifts near the local office, municipal office, in order to collect aid, humanitarian aid, and to give advice if needed. I was a member of that board myself, which lasted for about a week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not addressing humanitarian issues. I am interested in security issues. We have a case where Serbs have been expelled from Croatia, and they arrive and they are certainly displeased, which is quite understandable. In your village, there are Croats who live there also, so there might be a problem between those people who have been expelled and the Croats, who might be blamed for having taken part in these expulsions. At that time at the municipal level, since you held a position inside this municipality, did you warn the police or state authorities that certain measures needed to be taken to avoid any clashes, i.e., illegal occupation of flats or any form of mistreatment? Is or was there an awareness that problems could occur; any political speeches, any political decision? The clash between a great number of refugees and local residents, some of whom were of the same ethnicity as some of the refugees, did this lead to a particular awareness, i.e., that problems might occur?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now your question is much more clear, Your Honour. Yes, according to what I know, certain activities were conducted by local authorities, by the local council led by Dobrosav Markovic. He used to be a policeman. That was his occupation earlier, so he had contacts, he had acquaintances in the Secretariat of the Interior of Ruma Municipality. He would send delegations. He would go with delegations to the SUP to inform them about the situation and that there was a danger that things could escalate due to the large number of newly-arrived residents who had come to our village. There were also gatherings of residents held, devoted to this topic, where people were told that the situation needed to calm down so that there would be no escalation of problems. I personally took part in many such gatherings and sent reassuring, calming messages to refugees, because I understood their situation, I understood their displeasure and revolt or intolerance towards other ethnic group. Also, representatives of local authorities used to come or, rather, representatives of municipal authorities would come to these gatherings, so they were informed as well. Then there were the journalists, who informed the public about what was going on. The Socialist Party, who was in power at the time, also took certain steps in order to calm down tensions. A police station was even set up in our village precisely because of the danger that existed and incidents that had already occurred. We were also visited by leaders of various political parties from Vojvodina. They would come to gatherings in the beginning, calling upon citizens to remain calm and to find a way to coexist peacefully together, saying that there was sufficient space in Vojvodina, that there was no need for any violence or expelling of residents, as had happened in Croatia. However, none of this was sufficient, and we know what happened afterwards.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. You've answered my question in a very detailed way. What you've just said is very important. If I understand correctly, all the political parties were aware of what was happening, and amongst others, the Socialist Party which was in power. And you added something, and you said they set up a police office to deal with the problem. So all the political parties did what they needed to to avoid problems occurring. This is what I should infer from your answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, not entirely in that way. Most of them, yes, but the party that was in power, they did not engage themselves to a sufficient degree. I personally believe that the now two late presidents, Slobodan Milosevic and Tudjman, had a personal agreement to exchange the population, so I'm not fully convinced that the Socialist Party truly wanted to prevent this exchange of population. They just wanted to control the situation, to keep it under control, so as to avoid an armed conflict between local residents and refugees.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is very interesting. So according to you, at least in your opinion, Slobodan Milosevic and Mr. Tudjman had a personal agreement to exchange the population. This is really your opinion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that is what I believe, and most of the public too. I think it was published that there had been a secret agreement between the two of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a question. Witness, please, you told us that at one point in time some leaders of political parties came from Vojvodina to try and cool things down. Could you expound on this, please? Could you tell us exactly which leaders came from which party in order to cool things down?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, as far as I can remember, there was this lady who was a representative of the League of Social Democrats of Vojvodina. Then there was this gentleman who was a representative of the Hungarian Party and this joint Hungarian-Croat Party, and this other person whose name I cannot remember. I think that later on he was Minister of Agriculture, but I cannot remember exactly now what his name was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Was there also a leader from the Serbian Radical Party who came to cool things down?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At that rally, no.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I want you to bear in mind that the Serbian Radical Party did not exist then. The initiative committee was established only in April 1992. I'd just like to draw your attention to that fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I had noticed that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. Was there -- I can't remember the name of the movement, you know, the movement that was before the Serbian Radical Party, which brought together Serbian nationalists. Could you help me on this one, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, as far as I know, only the Serbian Renewal Movement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. That was the one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Did a leader from the Serbian Renewal Party also come, like all others, to cool things down? I think that was the reason behind the question put to you by Judge Lattanzi.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. Later on, they spoke up, just like their president Vuk Draskovic did. This was on the basis of my contacts with him and also through the Ruma board. In public, they made statements in order to cool the situation down, calm it down, and also treat the way -- treat the refugees differently.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So they did intervene, but a bit later; is that it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the representatives of the Serbian Renewal Movement did not come to the village officially to attend rallies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Maybe we have a bit taken up the questions that you wanted to put, Mr. Ferrara, but now you have the floor again.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Mr. Ejic, did Vojislav Seselj come to cool things down when he came in Hrtkovci?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: I don't think he came to cool things down. He did not call for violence when he spoke, but I don't think his intention was to cool things down. In public, he said he wanted to support reciprocity in conduct, that the Serb authorities should behave the same way towards non-Serbs who are not loyal, in his opinion, just as the Croatian authorities have been treating non-Croatians.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Can you tell us exactly when and where you saw him in Hrtkovci, of course?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: I first saw him on the 6th of May, 1992, when this one-and-only rally of the Serbian Radical Party was held in our village.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Was anyone escorting him or accompanying him?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: As far as I could see, I think that he came with three cars and that he had some trouble with his car, I think with the tire, in front of Dip Sava, a socially-owned enterprise at the time. So from that particular location to the stage where the rally was held, he came on foot, escorted by the people who were accompanying him.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: How would you describe these men who were accompanying him? Were they armed; how were they dressed?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: Well, the people who were with him, who were his personal escorts, were not armed. I only noticed a youngish person who had a knife at the belt. However, some other people, who came before he did, were armed. They walked through the centre of our village, that is to say, from the centre itself to the venue where the actual rally was held. That is to say that these people did not come with him, they arrived an hour before him, and they passed through our village on foot.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Did you witness any preparation for the arrival of Vojislav Seselj at the rally?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: Well, in passing, as the stage was being prepared just before he came, I was curious. I was interested in attending the meeting itself, so I did come. I walked around. I walked through the main street too, and that is how I noticed this group of people whom I did not know, who were wearing black clothing like the Chetniks in the Second World War. They had weapons, pistols, knives, also bandaliers. I think that their objective was to create fear, and a different psychological atmosphere among the local population just before the meeting -- the rally would start.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Was anyone with Seselj on the stage while he was giving his speech?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: Yes. As far as I can remember, Dr. Vojislav Seselj was the third speaker, the last speaker, after the introduction made by Blagoje Dudic, Zilic spoke, and then a lady. I think she was from Ruma or, rather, the Municipal Party Board from Ruma, I think. That's what I think. After the two of them, Vojislav Seselj spoke.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Let's start with the first speech. So the first one to speak was Blagoje Dudic; I'm right? Yes. What did he say?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I cannot remember exactly, but I think it was just a few introductory remarks, a speech of welcome, things like that. Immediately after that, Zilic spoke.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: What did Zilic say, and who is Zilic?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: Zilic is a refugee from Croatia, rather, Zagreb, who had come among the first refugees. After the violent takeover of power in the local commune, he was also on the council of the local commune. I know that after that, he left the village of Hrtkovci. I don't know exactly where it was that he went. I cannot recall exactly everything that he said, but what left a lasting imprint in my memory was the list of local inhabitants that he read out. He claimed that their children were in Croatia or, more precisely, they were members of the ZNG. He said that they were not loyal citizens of the Republic of Serbia and that there was no place for them in Hrtkovci. I remember that among these names, the following ones were mentioned. These were eminent citizens from the village, like Dr. Branko Vuksanic, then Lulic, Branimir Lulic, who was one of the farmers, then the director of Dip Sava, a socially-owned enterprise at the time, then the director of the cooperative in the village, and some other names that I cannot recall exactly. If you show me a document where the names are listed, I can put a circle around the names that were read out on that day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute, Witness. The speech which Mr. Seselj is going to give on that day is a very important element in the indictment, and therefore we, as Judges, must really be very careful regarding this speech. I'm just like a person that has to make an autopsy; I really have to look into everything and scrutinize everything. So before continuing with the content of the speech, I would like to know first what had motivated Mr. Seselj for coming to that place. Was he giving a speech that was part of an electoral campaign? Was he here to give a speech in order to promote himself? Did he come to give a speech in order to promote his party? Was the purpose to have a meeting or a rally with the population because of the problem connected with the Serbs that had been expelled from Croatia, or was there another reason to this meeting, to this rally? I mean, you were there, you were on the spot. You attended the rally, and you heard the speech, and I would like to know exactly what was the circumstances prevailing at the time. So could you try and enlighten us on this, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my opinion and belief is the following: A day or two earlier on, posters were put up and, it was broadcast on Radio Ruma that a promotion rally of the Serb Radical Party would be held in relation to the forthcoming elections. So Mr. Seselj, himself, spoke along those lines. However, what had happened before the rally itself is what I remember and what astonished me at the time and that led me to make a different conclusion, was the security provided for the rally itself. Every 100 metres, roughly, there was a policeman with an automatic rifle along the road or, rather, in the street. They were providing security for the group that passed there, the armed group that I described when I spoke previously. Traffic had been stopped from the center itself to Dip Sava, and the traffic was channeled through the back streets. That reminded me of the times when the late president Josip Broz would pass through. He had that kind of security. So I found that to be a bit strange. I never realised that an election rally could be secured in that way. That led me to conclude that this rally had some other intentions too. It wasn't just part of the election campaign, as had been made public.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The very impressive police machinery that had been set up, I presume that it was under -- they were reporting to Mr. Milosevic, weren't they? I believe that this decision must have been made at a very high level in order to place a great number of policemen at the disposal of this meeting; right? What can you say about this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree, exactly. I agree with you. This does make me believe and conclude that the authorities had very good information and representatives of state security in the village itself. That is how they organised this security, because they had assumed that there might be an armed conflict between the locals and the refugees and the participants in the rally itself. As for what I said during my previous remarks, namely, that in my view there had been an agreement between the two presidents, that was actually being carried out in practice. This kind of security provided led me to that conclusion too. I think that at the time Dr. Vojislav Seselj was a tool and that unconsciously he had been used by the then president, Mr. Slobodan Milosevic, or rather his regime.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I had an objection, but I didn't want to interrupt the answer being provided to your question. I would just like to draw your attention to the following: We haven't come to my speech yet. The witness has spoken about Milan Zilic's speech at the rally, so I'd like to draw your attention to that. Since the Prosecutor proffered the entire content of the rally here as evidence, I think that this is unfair. I think that the Prosecutor should show the witness Milan Zilic's speech, and then we should compare the names mentioned by the witness and the names mentioned by the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute, Mr. Seselj. You want to discuss the content of the speeches of those who spoke before you, but I was trying to find out what had happened earlier. I wanted to know exactly what was the motivation for this rally to be held, and I wanted to know what were the circumstances prevailing. And the witness has provided us with a wealth of details. I believe that during the cross-examination, you can come back on certain things which I thought were extremely interesting and very enlightening. Mr. Ferrara is asking questions on what the others said before you. This is where we were, and I will now give the floor to Mr. Ferrara, again apologising for having interrupted him. I really wondered what were the motivations for the rally. But, Mr. Ferrara, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: The names that you mentioned before, the names mentioned by Zilic, do you know their ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do. They were Croats and Hungarians.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: What happened to them later?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: Most of those who had been mentioned at the rally later moved away or, rather, exchanged their houses with the Serbs who had come from Croatia. One person remained, Lulic. I think that he's one of the people from that list who had not carried out an exchange, who rather went on living in Hrtkovci, Branimir Lulic.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Your Honours, do we want to start now with the analysis of the speech of Vojislav Seselj or do you want to have a break before, which is in five minutes. It will be longer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that we need to analyse Mr. Seselj's speech, of course, but we better have the break now. That way, we can discuss the content of the speech after the break. Let's break for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The court is back in session. Mr. Ferrara, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: So, Mr. Ejic, let's move to the speech held by Dr. Seselj. So after this Zilic, who spoke after Mr. Zilic?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: The lady from Ruma. I can't remember her name.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: And what did she say?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: I don't think I actually remember that. I cannot remember exactly what it was that she said.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Can you describe for the Trial Chamber, to the best of your memory, exactly what Vojislav Seselj said during his speech?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: Dr. Vojislav Seselj, when he took the floor, first had an objection, in terms of the loudspeaker, and he asked for the persons gathered there to get closer to the stage. Access to the stage was restricted. There was a ribbon there by way of an obstacle. And then he asked for it to be removed so that people could get as close as possible to the stage. He also said that there weren't that many people present, so they could get closer to the stage. After the usual greeting, "Brothers and sisters, Serbs," he moved on briefly. He spoke of his programme. I can't remember his words exactly, I can't remember the details, but it was the usual thing, what he said on television and in other situations. What I remember well is the following: Since he did not criticise the list that was read out by Zilic, in that way he actually supported the first speaker, along with a remark that he or, rather, his party also knew the names of the children who were in the ZNG, children from Hrtkovci who were members of the ZNG, people who had dodged mobilisation into the Yugoslav Army, in his view, since he stated then that he advocated reciprocity in conduct, as far as the Serb authorities were concerned. He said that all disloyal ethnic Croats and Hungarians whose children were in Croatia -- rather, in the ZNG, there was actually no place for them in Hrtkovci. He also added that they would be more humane; namely, that they would organise bus transportation for them, sandwiches, and take them to the Croatian border that way, as opposed to the Tudjman regime and the way it treated the Serb population in Croatia. And then the comment was that they can go on foot to their homeland, meaning Croatia, all of those who were loyal. And then he added that according to his information, there were Hungarian residents who have responded to the calls and were loyal citizens of Serbia and were loyal to the authorities of Serbia, that there was no reason for them to fear, that they would enjoy his protection even, and that he expected them to win in the local and federal elections, and that they would thus implement their policies which were announced in their programme.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Did Vojislav Seselj name anybody in his speech?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: I can't remember. I don't think he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Did he name again the same people that were mentioned before by Mr. Zilic?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: He didn't name these people, but he said that he had information that certain residents or, rather, their children were members of the ZNG, thus showing support to that list, but he doesn't name anyone from that list.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: How long was the speech?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, some ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: How many people attended this rally?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: As for residents, themselves, there were not that many. Perhaps some people from that street where the stage was, and maybe some people from the main street. Most of the residents were busy with agricultural works, since that was the main activity in the village, but there were a lot of people from neighbouring towns, from Ruma and neighbouring villages. I base that conclusion on having seen people whom I know from Ruma who came to the rally, and I think that there were a total of 300 attending the rally.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Were there many refugees?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: Yes. Most were refugees, people from elsewhere, and residents, local residents, were a minority.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Was Ostoja Sibincic present at the speech?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: Yes, he was. He stood on the side of the stage. He was an organiser, together with Mr. Momic, Blagoje Dudic and other refugees and members of the Serbian Radical Party.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: How would you describe the audience response to Seselj's speech?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: Well, there was acclamation, ovations, applause. I think that there were even slogans, "Ustashas out," chanted. I can't remember other details.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Were there specific words or phrases used by Mr. Seselj that generated this kind of response, this acclamation or this slogan?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: I think that the following was said, "Let them go to their homeland," meaning Croatia, and this is what caused ovations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, you yourself, did you stay there, did you stand there, did you boo, did you -- what did you actually do, personally?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I expressed no reaction whatsoever. I stood some ten metres from the stage. I simply observed the reaction of other people. I observed them. I expected such reactions.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, can we please see the Exhibit 65 ter number 1274 on the screen. It's the transcript of Mr. Seselj's speech mentioned before by Mr. Seselj, extracted from his book "The Hrtkovci Affair."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, once again I insist on looking at the entire document, that is to say, both the speech of Milan Zilic and my speech. The names listed here by the witness do not correspond to the names given by Milan Zilic. None of the names correspond, and I don't -- I think that's important because the Prosecutor has to try to establish the truth, no matter what the truth is, even if it goes against the indictment, to its detriment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, we have a text which is an excerpt from Mr. Seselj's book. Mr. Seselj admittedly has written a number of books, and it seems that this book contains the speeches of Mr. Seselj and Mr. Zilic's speech also. This is something you can check on the screen, because you have the text in your language on the screen. According to what Mr. Seselj says, the names that were quoted in his speech are names which do not match the names which appear here and there. What do you have to say to this? Look at this yourself. You can see the names. The Stepic brothers, the Sindric brothers, Paso Mladen, Mata Markus, Ivica Sostaric, Fortnet, Nemet, and others.

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't see the names. In the very beginning, May elections, and then it says "Ziric." I don't see that here.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, perhaps the third paragraph could be enlarged and zoomed in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please look at the third paragraph. I've read it in English, but you can see it in the Serbian version in Cyrillic.

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: It says here: "Dozens of young men, the Grdic brothers, Stepic brothers, Sindric brothers, Raso Mladen, Mata Marcus, Ivica Sostaric, Mr. Fortnet, and Mr. Nemet and others." Now that I have read this, I remember that they were mentioned as well as the names on the list, and then in my evidence, I mentioned another two or three names. It doesn't say "Samo, Mata," here, [indiscernible] "Grizelj," the director of the cooperative.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Dr. Vuksanic is missing, too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would you explain this, Witness? How do you explain this, unless the text in Mr. Seselj's book has been abridged or amputated? How is it that there are some of the names which you heard which could not appear in this text?

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Your Honours, can I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Ferrara.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Also in this speech, after his name, there is the category of others. Maybe we should know who are these others not mentioned in this book, after this long list of names, "Stepic brothers, Sindric brothers, Mladen, Markus, Sostaric, Fortnet, Nemet and others," so I think we should know who are those others, maybe the names mentioned by the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Ferrara, the issue is whether the text that has been published in Dr. Seselj's book is an accurate reflection of the speech held by Mr. Zilic.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Judge, it's not so accurate because there is the category in the book and others, so maybe Dr. Seselj should explain to us who are these other names mentioned during the speech.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Ferrara, you are right. Perhaps the expression "and others," i.e., those who picked up on the speech have decided to add "and others," but perhaps Mr. Seselj, in his speech, quotes all the names and then gets to Nemet and says, "and others." We don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I would like to draw your attention to the fact that this book was published before there was any hint that an indictment could be issued before -- against me by The Hague Tribunal, and the Prosecutor knows the exact title of the book and the date of its publishing, so he should tell us that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, I have one question. Last week, you told us that there were videos. As far as you know, was your speech recorded anywhere on an audiotape or not?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is footage of the speech, and this text was transcribed from the footage. There were no interventions. It was reproduced just as it was filmed. However, I do not have any communication with my associates, it has been banned, and I cannot obtain it anymore. I do not speak about my trial with anybody, except that I occasionally ask my family members about their impression from the broadcast that they see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, let's imagine that there is an audiotape which is authentic and which reflects what has been said and that the names that you have mentioned are not quoted in this tape. What would you have to say to that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The names that appear here on the screen before me were mentioned. I can't claim with 100 per cent certainty that all of them were mentioned, but I can confirm that one of the names that is not mentioned here was mentioned at the time. This man is alive to this day or, rather, lives there to this day. He's a farm worker.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's what you said a while ago. And if I remember correctly, he's called Ilic or something like that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Lulic, yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Exactly. I have a good memory, and I record everything in my brain. As far as you remember, Mr. Zilic purportedly quoted Lulic, and in this text Lulic is not mentioned. This is a mystery.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, correct. He was mentioned, as was the director of the Sava DIP and the director of the cooperative. They were mentioned, but they do not appear in this text.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, let me draw your attention to this: How come Lulic was mentioned when he never went to the ZNG, he never went to the regular Croatian Guards, nor did the director of the cooperative. The people that are mentioned here were the people that went to Tudjman's army to fight against the Serbian people. That was the essence of this speech, not just mentioning all Croats residing in this village.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, we have already come across this problem when another witness came to testify. Mr. Zilic quotes some names of residents of your village who join the ZNG, the Croatian National Guards, and he quotes a whole series of names. This is what we can understand. Then, according to you, comes Lulic. Why is Lulic mentioned if he is not a member of the ZNG? This is why this is a mystery. Are you quite sure that you can rely on your memory 100 per cent?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. You mentioned a secret, Your Honour. That's precisely what it was about, that prominent residents were mentioned, directors of certain enterprises who later on were the first to be -- or, rather, to exchange their properties, thus prompting other residents to do the same. So the point was to intimidate and to make the population start with the exchanges. The people who are on the list, the names --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I understand what you are saying, and what you are saying is extremely important. So either, according to your theory, if Mr. Zilic quotes names and then those people need to leave their flats or their houses because they can no longer stay, this is in line with the indictment, or the other theory would have it another way, and the Bench needs to address all possibilities. The speech only addressed those Croats that had joined the ZNG or were going to join the ZNG, and that is another issue altogether. The text published by Mr. Seselj, according to him, seems to match the audio version which he has and which the Prosecution seemingly does not have. The audio version does perhaps not mention Lulic anywhere, but if the audio version has been tampered with, then it wouldn't appear. This is extremely important. Are you quite sure that Lulic was mentioned? Are you 100 per cent certain of this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. It's on the transcript. Mr. Ferrara.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Your Honours, just to be clear, the accused said that this book was published before the indictment was issued. According to the information that the Prosecution has, the book was published in 2004, not before the indictment was issued but after.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's not true, Mr. President. This was published twice. The first time, it was published as part of my collected works, and then the second time it was published in 2004 as part of the book "Devil's Associate." So that was the second time in 2004. I provided to the Prosecution, in 2003, a set of my entire works, and it was handed over to them in this courtroom. You can see this recorded in the transcripts from status conferences. So all of these books, 80 of them in total, were published long before I arrived in The Hague.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Ferrara, I remember that Mr. Seselj had told us that he had handed over dozens of books to the OTP, so if we're not mistaken, there are two books where his speech is mentioned, the book of 2004 - that's straightforward here, you are right - but it seems that there is also another one that was published earlier. We can't check this right now, but I believe that you will have ample time to check that, as well as Mr. Seselj. He will also have ample time to prove whatever he wants to prove. So please continue, Mr. Ferrara.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Mr. Ejic, could you continue to read the speech, the second -- I think that we should move to the second page.

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I may add something about these names that are mentioned by Mr. Zilic. I saw the name here "Raso Mladen." As far as I know, there was a man, Raso, in my street who now lives and works in Austria. And then there were the Stepic brothers, if we are referring to the same Stepic brothers. One lives in Hrtkovci to this day, and the other one lives in Novi Sad. Then Sindric brothers, they have left. They had exchanged their houses. As for Sostaric, there is a family under that last name. One brother lives in Hrtkovci, the other one in Ruma, but I doubt that they could have been members of the ZNG if they live in Hrtkovci to this day, providing we are speaking of the same Stepic brothers or Sostaric brothers. I would like to deny that, what Zilic had read, he could not have had information, nor did he know these people or their children. I think that this list has been put together by Sibincic and the others, and this is how these names came to be here. That's what I wanted to add. This is my opinion concerning the names mentioned here.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Do you remember if --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, I have an objection. Mr. President, I think that you need to intervene, now that there is this attempt to turn things upside down. We're not speaking about whether all the information in the speech of Milan Zilic was accurate or not. We're speaking of what Zilic uttered. Did he say what is mentioned in his speech, as is reproduced in this document, or are we speaking about something else? Zilic is not accused here for uttering things are not accurate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, I know that you're a university professor. I know that university professors love to lecture, but please refrain from lecturing and don't lecture the Prosecutor and don't lecture the Judges or lecture the Presiding Judge. Don't lecture him and tell him what he's supposed to do. This is unacceptable behaviour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, absolutely, there was no need for you to make your objection. I had fully understood that the witness was making his own appreciation of the reason that had motivated Zilic for mentioning these names. I mean, that's his opinion. We all understood that, so don't raise an objection for that. He explained that this had been done voluntarily, and he is mentioning other people, blaming other people, notably Sibincic, for example, but please continue, Mr. Ferrara.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, I think we have exhausted the contents of Zilic's speech, but there is one thing I would like you to clarify before we move on to Mr. Seselj's speech, and that is: The name that is indicated in the book, it seems to me here the name is Milan Ziric and not Zilic, and I just want to ensure that we're speaking about the same person.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think so. This is a translation from -- of course, I don't read Cyrillic, so I don't know what it is in Cyrillic, Zilic or Ziric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: No, no, in Cyrillic it's also "Ziric," as far as I can see, but can you clarify with the witness what the name of the person was?

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: What was the name? What's the name of this person, Mr. Ejic, Zilic or Ziric?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: Zilic. There's an "R" here. As far as I know, it was just Zilic. That's how he introduced himself, and now I remember that's his first name, too, Milan.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours -- or, rather Judges, this is a mistake, it is a typo. The people who were getting this typed up from the tapes didn't know the exact names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, I had also inferred that this was just a typo. Obviously, there is a problem here. The witness did say that the person's name was Zilic, Milan Zilic, and we see that there's an "R" written in the name. It must be a typo. That's marginal, anyway. What's important is that somebody called either Zilic or Ziric said all this. Mr. Ferrara, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Just a question about the first part of the speech. Did Mr. Zilic mention only people whose children were in the Croatian Army or also other people from Hrtkovci, to the best of your recollection?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: Other people too. That is what is missing in this list here, the names that I mentioned and added; Samo, Mata, and some others as well. I can't remember at this very moment. However, in addition to these names, he mentioned other names too. What was noted was that these were the last names and the first names of the children who were members of the ZNG, but he mentioned other names as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Let's move to the speech of Mr. Seselj. It should be the second page of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute. This lady whose name has not been identified and who introduces Mr. Seselj, when we look at things closely, this lady seems to be well informed of Mr. Seselj's programme. She knows exactly who Mr. Seselj is. So she sums up Mr. Seselj's actions very well. But this lady, did she come from -- is she a local or did she come from the outside, and did she come just in order to introduce the main speaker? As far as you recollect, could you tell us what happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The lady is not from our village. I think she's from Ruma.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] She was not known by the population of Hrtkovci; they didn't know her?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Ferrara, let's move on to the speech.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: So, Mr. Ejic, can you read the speech on your own, of course, of Mr. Seselj and tell us faithfully what you remember you heard that day? Of course, you should focus on the part regarding Hrtkovci, not the entire political programme of the party.

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: I beg your pardon. Do you want me to read this? You want me to read it out loud or should I read it to myself?

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: No, to yourself. Let us know when you want Mr. Registrar to change -- flip the pages. If you feel more comfortable with another copy, we can provide you with a paper copy instead of reading it on the screen.

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: There is no need for that. I can find my way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Ferrara, I assume that during the proofing, you showed him the speech. He knows the speech; right?

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Witness, can we move to page 4 of the speech. That is the part regarding -- concerning Hrtkovci. The English version is page 4; the third paragraph, page 4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Ferrara, you're moving to page 4, and you intend to go back to the previous pages later, because if not, I have a question on page 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, please, on page 3 Mr. Seselj is going to talk about General Kadijevic and actually blame him. According to him, he's an American spy, but I believe that this Kadijevic has just been awarded Russian nationality, just a few weeks ago. So he is really questioning General Kadijevic. He's saying he's a traitor and blaming him. Did you hear this? And if you really heard it, isn't it because Mr. Seselj was contesting the GNA apparatus and even challenging Milosevic, who at the time was president of Serbia and therefore was in charge of the army? So how can you -- how do you assess this question, because I believe it's a very essential question, a very essential sentence in this speech. It really helps us assess the entire situation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot remember exactly this part of the speech because my attention was not focused on the speech itself that much because through the media I was already familiar enough with what it was that Dr. Vojislav Seselj was saying. I was more focused on the reaction of the audience. I didn't really pay that much attention to the entire speech.
