This part where there is a reference to Mr. Kadijevic, well, I think that that is being brought into question, as you yourself have said, Your Honour, but I cannot recall that particular part. I think it was mentioned, but I'm not 100 per cent sure that I heard it then at the rally or whether I heard it on TV.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, thank you. Mr. Ferrara, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. So let's move to page 4. It is the part where Mr. Seselj mentioned what's happening in Hrtkovci. It's paragraph - third paragraph and fourth paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Please, can you read them, these two paragraphs, and tell us if you -- exactly what you remember you heard that day or if it is missing -- something missing in this transcript.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I demand that the witness read this part out loud. It is important for the public. It is the key part of the speech, as far as the indictment is concerned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're demanding. You're not here to demand anything. Then, you know, the text is on the screen. The witness can see it. On page 4 of the English version, this is paragraph 3. So I believe that the Serbian version is also displayed. Witness, have you read the paragraph dealing with the village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay. He's fully aware, so please go ahead, Mr. Ferrara.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I can say is the following: I remember certain passages, but I do not remember all of what is stated in this text, except for parts of individual sentences. As I've already mentioned in response to one of the questions put to me by Your Honour, all of those who were not loyal had nothing to do in Hrtkovci any longer, those whose children were in the ZNG. And then the last part: "Brother and sister Serbs, if Tudjman expelled more than 200.000 Serbs, a part of them will return to the area of the Serb Krajina, but another part cannot."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The paragraph starting: "In this village ..." is an essential paragraph because it is at the very heart of the Prosecution's case. For everyone to be fully aware of this, including the public following the hearing, please read the paragraph out loud. Please read it out loud.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Your Honour: "In this village, Hrtkovci, in this place in Serbian Srem, there is no room for Croats. Who are the only Croats for whom there is room among us? Only those Croats and their families who have shed blood together with us on the front-lines. Anyway, they were called Croats in name only. They have already awakened to the fact that they are, in fact, Catholic Serbs. Some of them even served with our volunteers. They will stay here with us, whereas all the rest must clear out of Serbia, including those from here, from Hrtkovci, who locked up their houses and left, reckoning, I suppose, that they will come back one day. But our message to them is: You have nowhere to return to. Serbian refugees will move into their houses." Shall I go on? Shall I read the rest?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, thank you. This was very useful. Mr. Ferrara.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Do you remember this part of the speech?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: I remember, but not entirely and not in the form of such sentences. Rather, since this was a very long time ago and it did not remain in my memory, what does remain in my memory is this advocacy of reciprocity. Then the families whose children were in the ZNG had no room in Hrtkovci. All the rest should not be afraid. No one would touch them. That pertained to the neighbouring localities as well, not only Hrtkovci.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: So what message did you take away from the speech?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: What does the word "loyal" mean and how would it be interpreted by refugees who were expelled from Croatia? In their minds, this word would be interpreted in different ways. Would they check the accuracy of the allegations read out by Zilic, for instance, or those presented by Dr. Vojislav Seselj or some other speaker? That was the key thing. I believe that actually this was a message to them to the effect of, "Judge things for yourself and you know what you should do. You've been expelled. You have nowhere to go, whereas Croats and Hungarians are living here. Carry out an exchange with them." That was my understanding of this, of these words, and that is what I took away with me from the rally. Of course, part of it had to do with propaganda for the party programme itself and attacking and accusing Milosevic. This was a marginal issue, as far as I was concerned. I did not believe that this was the essence and the main point for which this rally in Hrtkovci was organised.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, we've already seen videos showing Mr. Seselj making speeches. No one will contest that Mr. Seselj is an excellent speaker. But as far as you remember, when he said -- when he made this speech, was he reading or was he improvising? You held a political position, you've already made speeches probably, so I'm sure you're well aware of this. So do you think this was an improvised speech or was it a well-thought-out speech with every word been carefully weighted before being said? And just to top off my question: In the speech, I see "Serbian brothers and sisters" cropping up over and over again. It comes up at the beginning of some paragraphs. So one can really wonder about all this. Do you believe this was an improvised speech or a well-thought-out speech with every word having been very carefully weighted and scrutinised?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In my opinion, Your Honour, I think this was a usual sort of speech, but with the intention that was there. It is practice, as far as the speaker is concerned, to address refugees in this way precisely in order to win over their trust and to show his compassion with the problem they are facing. The speech was not read out; that is to say, it was an impromptu speech, and I believe that he had conceived of it earlier and prepared it for the rally itself. The usual term used by Dr. Vojislav Seselj is one that he used at rallies of citizens in order to calm them down and to win over their trust. I even did it myself, "Brothers and sisters, Serbs," or "polmazebog, may God help us, brothers and sisters, Serbs" and the refugees would always greet that with ovations and pleasure. This is something that they really liked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Can you read the next paragraph, paragraph 4 of the same page, also loud if you like?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: It's the last one, isn't it? "Brothers and sisters Serbs, if Tudjman has expelled more than 200.000 Serbs, part of them will return to the area of the Serb Krajina, but another part cannot settle there. We have to give those Serbs a roof over their heads and we have to feed hungry mouths. We have no money to build new housing. We do not have the capacity ..." And now the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: " ... to create new jobs for them. Very well, then. If we cannot do that, then every Serb family of refugees should be given the address of a Croatian family. The police will give it to them. The police will do as the government decides, and we will soon be in government. Fine, then. Every Serb family of refugees will come to a Croat door and give the Croats they find there their address in Zagreb or other Croatian towns. Oh, yes, they will, they will. There will be enough buses. We will drive them to the border of Serbian territory, and they can walk on from there if they do not leave before of their own accord. "Some traitors of the Serb people in Belgrade --"

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: You can stop here. Do you remember what you have read?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: I remember these sentences, but I cannot say with 100 per cent certainty that that is what I heard on that day at the rally or whether I heard that on television. I'm not 100 per cent sure, but I remember part of these sentences, I remember hearing them, things like: "We will get into power," and the sentence: "We are going to give addresses to refugees," and others.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, the paragraph that you have just read is a paragraph I would like to link with what you had just said about the secret pact that would have been made between Milosevic and Tudjman. So either there is a secret pact, and if that is so, if Mr. Seselj agrees with Mr. Milosevic, he would say that Croats must return home, without saying that this will be in the framework of an exchange of flats, but what really strikes me here is that in the sentence he actually utters, he says, "When we will be in power, if we are in power." It seems that he assumes that a Croat could go to Zagreb to take a flat only when the Serbian Radical Party will decide or will be in government. But then this does not match the theory of the secret pact between Milosevic and Tudjman, including, you know -- with the participation of Mr. Seselj. So could you enlighten us on this, because you came up with this idea. This might be a bit complex. I'm just trying to understand and to move forward.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this opinion of mine, this assertion of mine, is based on everything that was happening in our village. If the police which existed there at the time did not do its job properly, as it was supposed to, if the authorities did not provide accommodation to the refugees in state-owned, socially-owned institutions or, rather, public hotels, socially-owned hotels and other available facilities for housing, rather they sent them -- or rather they allowed them to stay in our village and elsewhere, too, where there was a majority of ethnic Croats and Hungarians. Then that proves my thesis that there had been such an agreement. As for the very beginning, when all of this started happening, as far as Dr. Vojislav Seselj is concerned, I think that he had convictions of his own and a national programme too, and that basically he lived in the past. Because of some of the things that had happened in the Second World War, he was in favour of a certain revengism and his energy was aimed in that direction; indeed to have this secret agreement carried through. I think that later he became part of the federal government, which is confirmed by -- which, rather, is a confirmation of my thesis that there had been this kind of a plan, an agreement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This was your view, that there had been an agreement between Tudjman and Milosevic, with participation of Seselj as well, or only between Milosevic and Tudjman?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the very outset, Your Honours, I think that it was an agreement between the two late presidents and that later Seselj joined Milosevic and that he was unwittingly used by Milosevic for such a plan. Milosevic used him to organise many volunteers to participate in the conflict in Croatia. That is my opinion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To be more precise, do you think that Mr. Seselj was Mr. Milosevic's puppet or instrument, or do you believe that he used Mr. Seselj, knowing full well what he was doing? Could you specify, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Your Honours, I think that in the beginning he was used as a person who had expressed great interest for the problem of Serbs expelled from Croatia. He wanted to provide assistance and manpower by organising volunteers, and then later on, when all of this unfolded, he became aware and accepted the plan of population exchange. He did that via his activities and appearances on television through his published works and so on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection. I have an impression that this witness has been upgraded to an expert. He has secondary education. He's a farm worker from a village, and he can only testify to things that he personally saw, heard, or experienced. Now he's testifying about global politics, about a secret agreement between Milosevic and Tudjman, and my subsequent joining that agreement. I think that this is incredible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, it's for the Bench to weigh all of this. Your comment is on the transcript, but it is the Bench that will determine the relevance and probative value of what he's saying. Please proceed, Mr. Ferrara.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Mr. Ejic, can we move to the last part of the speech, exactly the last paragraph. It should be page 8 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: What I have here is: "Brothers and sisters, Serbs ..." Is that what you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: The last one, starting with: "I firmly believe ..." The English version, the third paragraph: "I firmly believe that you Serbs from Hrtkovci ..."

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: What I have on the screen now I think is what you want. Can you please put the question? Should I read this out loud or what?

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Yes, read it out loud, please, the last paragraph.

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: "I firmly believe that you Serbs from Hrtkovci and from other villages in the vicinity will also know how to preserve your harmony and unity, that you will promptly get rid of the remaining Croats in your village and the vicinity; that you will know how to appreciate the fruits of freedom and democracy, that united we shall win, unite all the Serbian lands and overcome the economic and social crisis. To conclude today's promotion of the Serbian Radical Party, I salute you with the traditional Serbian greeting, 'All for the Serb cause, the Serb cause for all. Serbia will live on as long as her children are true to her.' Cheers."

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Do you remember the last part of the speech, after you hear the sentence, "To get rid of the Croats," of course?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: Unfortunately, I can't remember that sentence: "As for others, Serbia will live on as long as her children are true to her." I remember that one. I can't confirm "willful certainty" at the very beginning. Unfortunately, I just don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: I'd like to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We'll give it an exhibit number. Registrar, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit number P547.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd like now to move in closed session because I'd like to discuss with the witness one document coming from the Serbian archives. And according to your recent decision --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Let's move into closed session for a few moments.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: So, Mr. Ejic, I put the same question again. Do you know why Hrtkovci was selected as the centre for the rally of the Serbian Radical Party? You have to repeat what you said in private session.

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: It is my opinion that Hrtkovci was selected as the main location for the events that are being referred to, is based on a fact, something that happened in the Second World War. A column of prisoners from Serbia, from Sabac specifically, that was moving towards Belgrade and went through Hrtkovci, was not even given water. The locals were not allowed to give them even water or food. Actually, what was being bandied about was that these were Ustashas, because during the war this was the territory of the so-called independent state of Croatia, and the inhabitants of Hrtkovci even threw hot water at the prisoners, and they certainly wouldn't give them water to refresh themselves. My information speaks to the contrary; namely, that all of this is not correct and that there were examples of the contrary, that the local population threw apples and things like that to them, not hot water, and that German soldiers were preventing them from doing this. So there was this accusation bandied about in the public, in relation to Hrtkovci, that the inhabitants treated the prisoners from Serbia that were moving in a column inhumanely. I think that is the reason why Hrtkovci was chosen as a target, under quotation marks, and that that is why this was a focal point for organising the rally.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, what you're saying is quite interesting and maybe could be an explanation, but then why do you explain that Mr. Seselj, who has great knowledge of historical events and who often refers to events that occurred during World War II, did not mention this incident during -- in his speech? I mean, he could have said, "Dear brothers and sisters, I came here because this happened earlier," and this or that, and he does not mention all that. So how could you explain all of this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I cannot say why he didn't refer to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Ferrara, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Mr. Ejic, you said at the beginning of your testimony that there was an increasing of the illegal activity, of occupation of the house, after this rally. Do you remember if some -- any citizen assembly was held after this rally?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: I remember that after that rally, I don't know what the exact date was, but there were several rallies that were held -- sorry, not rallies, gatherings that were held of citizens in relation to the problems that cropped up.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Did you attend any of them, any of these gatherings?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: Yes. I, myself, attended one of these gatherings, and I was even one of the organisers of one such gathering, in terms of it having been scheduled. However, Ostoja Sibincic took advantage of that, together with the assembled refugees, and he came to the gathering and said that he had scheduled it. On that occasion, there was this verbal clash between him and myself. When I assessed the situation and when I realised that there may even be a physical showdown, I asked the locals that we leave the premises and hold this gathering in front of the building, and we adopted certain conclusions and sent our proposals to the municipal authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: I want to show you this press article at 65 ter number 1593. Please, Mr. Registrar, if you can put it on the screen.

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: I can see it on the screen, if that's it. "Ostoja threatens the traitors."

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Did you attend this meeting mentioned in this press article?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: I think that I did not attend this gathering, but I remember reading this in the newspapers, and I heard about it from quite a few local people who had also read about it, but also those who had attended the gathering themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Did you attend any similar meeting like this?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: Well, I attended many rallies of citizens that were similar, similar to this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Were you also to speak during these meetings?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did speak, I did take part.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Did Ostoja Sibincic give any speech during this meeting?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: At the meetings that I attended, Ostoja Sibincic did not make speeches. It was others who did, Rade Cakmak, and I can't remember all their names now. I remember him. However, there is something of interest in relation to Sibincic, if that is important for you. Would you like me to say it or --

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: I don't know what you want to say.

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: Well, there was this situation that actually led to something that did happen in practice; namely, I was nearby when Sibincic himself, after such a rally, said to the refugees, "You just go ahead and break into the houses that are free and available, write up documents as if you had signed a contract with the owners, and that will suffice as far as the police is concerned. No one will be able to do anything to you." For me, this meant instigation, and from that moment onwards the two of us distanced ourselves from each other and had different activities in the future, because I was absolutely opposed to that, whereas he was one of the organisers and one of the people who actually conceived of such events.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, Witness. Do you mean that some contracts were fake contracts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's what it means.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Was Ostoja Sibincic a member of the SRS?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that, that he was at the time. I know that nowadays he's a member of the Serb Radical Party. What I know is that he was in the SPO together with me and that later on he left the SPO, and for a while he was a member of the Socialist Party of Serbia. Now, as of late, as far as I know, he's in the Serb Radical Party.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: You mentioned before Rade Cakmak. Who is this guy, who is Rade Cakmak?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: Rade Cakmak is a refugee from Grubisno Polje, to the best of my knowledge. He is a person who spoke at such rallies, who took part in the violence that was brought against the inhabitants of Hrtkovci, who was accused and, I believe, convicted of having committed such things, he and his son and some others, I believe, in that group. He is also among those who unlawfully, illegally, moved into the house of a Hungarian, Andrija Cergi [phoen], who later either sold or exchanged his house. I know that the man lives in Hungary, and he worked in Austria and Germany, and I think that part of his family is also employed in Austria and Germany.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: In this article on the screen, please, can you read the first line, exactly the first line? No, in the title.

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: The title is: "Ostoja Threatens the Traitors."

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: And above it?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: "Citizens Assembly in Hrtkovci (Srbislavci)." "Srbislavci" is in brackets.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Can you explain as what does that mean, in brackets, "Srbislavci"?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: "Srbislavci" means that at the time the name of Hrtkovci was changed into Srbislavci. Even sign posts were placed at exit and entry points. This was done by the local commune. They passed a decision to that effect. At that time, he was the president of Srbislavci/Hrtkovci or, rather, the local commune. At that time, it was called the Council of the Local Commune. And he became that by force and unlawfully, under quotation marks, "at a citizens rally" that was mostly attended by refugees and neighbours from neighbouring villages rather than the inhabitants of Hrtkovci itself, because according to the law, the Council of the Local Commune is elected by the local population of Hrtkovci, not those who are not. However, he took advantage of the situation. As he spread fear among the population, the inhabitants no longer responded to invitations to attend -- to attend Assembly meetings because they didn't want to go through the threats that were addressed there. So this would be my explanation of Srbislavci, in brackets. It was his idea to change the name of the place.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Can you explain what -- of course, we don't speak B/C/S. Can you explain, what does it mean, "Hrtkovci," and what does it mean, "Srbislavci"?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: Well, "Hrtkovci" is an old name that has been there since the inception of Hrtkovci. It's been a long, long time. As far as I know and on the basis of what is written in some books, there were many dogs, "hrt," hounds. Perhaps that is how the village got its name, "Hrtkovci," whereas "Srbislavci" is based on the following association; that the majority population are Serbs and therefore the village should be called Srbislavci.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd like to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute. Before we move to admitting this document, Witness, I have a few questions to ask about what Mr. Sibincic is saying. He says that he will order that a policeman no longer has access to the village. I also note that the primary school is being rebaptized, is to be "Vladimir Nazor" and is going to change and be called now "Vuk Karadzic." I also note that Zelica Tkalac, the teacher, who is a Serb married to a Croat, will be forbidden from teaching. At least that's what was proposed to the population. Is that what he was asking the population to do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, may I just correct you on one point. The elementary school that was called "Vladimir Nazor" is now called "Milos Srnjanski" [phoen] rather than "Vuk Karadzic." A street is called "Vuk Karadzic Street." In relation to the proposal made by Sibincic in connection with the village itself, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. It seems, according to this document, that he was also in a mixed marriage, or several mixed marriages, actually. He was first married to a Hungarian and then to a Macedonian woman, which did not prevent him from opposing people who are also in a mixed marriage. As inhabitants of the village, that's the situation you perceived, and from this Sibincic, that's what he was actually professing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I know Mr. Sibincic, Your Honour, he does have an illegitimate child with a Macedonian woman, also an illegitimate child with a Hungarian woman; and now he lives with another Macedonian woman with whom he also has a child. His motives were of an economic nature. I think that most of the things he did, he did in order to benefit from them in material terms. I think this can be corroborated by a great deal of evidence, in terms of what happened in practice; namely, he took money from refugees in order to make houses available to them and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The document dates -- comes from -- is dated in August. Now, in August, when Sibincic proffers all this, I would like to know whether, to your knowledge, he was a member of the Serbian Radical Party or not.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no information indicating that he was a member of the Radical Party at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When he states all this, which hat does he have on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was his custom, when it comes to his political opponents and those who think differently from him or who oppose and who state publicly what is going on in villages, it was his custom to call them traitors or Ustashas. He also branded me a traitor. I even heard that in one of the gatherings that he had organised with refugees, a death sentence was issued to me. Allegedly, a refugee volunteered to carry that sentence out. I heard that from the late Momic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand what you're saying, but when Sibincic was asking of the sort -- when he was acting of the sort, was he doing this individually, just because that's his own personality and he's got this tendency to call everyone a traitor, and was saying all this to others who were not against what he was saying, or was he acting in the framework of an organisation, a party, or a group of individuals?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Partially in person, individually, and partially within a group, within an organisation; that is to say, he gathered refugees around him. He even had contacts -- I suppose, I'm not 100 per cent sure, but the facts indicate that people came from elsewhere, from Serbia, from Sabac, to exert pressure on the local population.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What you've just said is interesting. He was surrounded by a group of refugees, so he's a person, according to what I understand, who set up this group, this organisation. What I wanted to know is this: Was he the person who acted and set up this organisation on an individual basis or was this ordered from outside, somebody who told him that he needed to do this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is my belief that he did not come up with all of this on his own; rather, that he had instructions from the authorities. At the time, it was the regime of Slobodan Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, according to you, he got his instructions from the regime at that time. This is what you've just told us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's exactly right, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, what does the Serbian Radical Party have to do in all of this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Serbian Radical Party, under the circumstances, since after their founding most of their members were refugees, I see them as an accomplice. I see the party as an accomplice in all of these events.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sure that Mr. Seselj will address this again during his cross-examination, I assume. Mr. Ferrara, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Did you have the opportunity to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment, Mr. Ferrara. Let's give this document an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit number P549.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: That's the last question regarding this document, Your Honours. I forgot it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Stop. We are in open session. We shall have to redact this.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Sorry, I forgot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Let's move into private session and then you can put your question. This shall be redacted. When you are a Presiding Judge, you need to be on the ball at all times.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Did you have the opportunity --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Ferrara. We're now in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Mr. Ejic, did you at the time discuss with the refugees who instructed them to go to your village, who instructed them to go just to Hrtkovci?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: Well, I had occasion to talk to some refugees that I didn't know, and I learned from them that they had received instructions or, rather, information when they crossed the border that they should take the road to Sabac and that in Hrtkovci there were numerous vacant homes, and that there were homes there that could be exchanged. So who could have told them this at the border crossing? Either the police or some other officials.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Did they say you if they received any -- this kind of instruction from a particular political party?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Can you tell us what happened after the rally of the SRS on the 6th of May, 1992? Can you tell us the proportion of Serbs and non-Serbs living in Hrtkovci after this period? Was there a particular change in this proportion?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: I apologise. Your question is not entirely clear to me. What residents do you have in mind? You mean their ethnicity or what?

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: The citizens of Hrtkovci, not the refugees. Did it change the composition, the ethnic composition, because you say at the beginning of your testimony that in Hrtkovci, usually the Croats were the majority, 60 per cent or more, if I remember right. Did this change after the 6th of May, 1992?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: Now I understand the question. Yes, that is true, that after the rally, the departure and the exchange of homes intensified, the exchange of homes of Croats and some Hungarians with refugees from Croatia, so that the current situation is quite different from the situation prior to this. Percentage-wise, it would be as follows: In Hrtkovci, there used to be about 10 or so per cent of Serbs, including the Romas, and the rest were Croats and Hungarians. Nowadays, the number of Serbs or those of Orthodox faith increased, and the number of Croats is reduced, and to some extent of the Hungarians as well. In percentages, the picture would be as follows: About 20-some per cent are Hungarians, 10 to 15 per cent are Croats, and the rest are Serbs and the Roma.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Do you know -- do you personally know any family who are -- that was forced to leave Hrtkovci? Or not "family"; of course, single persons.

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: I want to show you a long list of names. If, Mr. Registrar, can you put on the screen the document number 2859. That is the annex 11 to the third amended indictment, coming from the annex to the expert report, the Ewa Tabeau expert report, and annex A, the list of persons who left Hrtkovci.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Mr. Ferrara, could we have the page number, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: The ERN number is -- page 37 out of 66.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Please, you can read this long list of names, and with the pen that you have there, if you can circle the names of people that you know were forced to leave Hrtkovci in that period of time. There should be a pen there. The usher will instruct you. Circle or line, what is easier.

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: Can we go on?

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Can we go to the other page? It's a list of 28 pages, so it will take time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Ferrara, if he needs to leaf through these 28 pages, he will come up with hundreds of names. He won't be able to do this. How many names will he target?

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Your Honours, he target about 60 or 70 names during the proofing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let him target these names, then.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Maybe more.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Further on, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Registrar has just told me that he had better circle these names. Draw a circle.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Tell us when you mark somebody.

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: Number 69 and 70, [marks]. [Marks] Number 209. The next number I circled is number 209, "Fumic, Marko."

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Do you know any other members of the Fumic family?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I know his brother, Milan, and I know their wives. I know the Fumic family.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Where were they force to do leave to?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: Nowadays they live in Podravska Slatina.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: But at the time, were they forced to leave, in 1992? We want to know if they were forced to leave in 1992, not now if they live in Hrtkovci. Maybe now some of them returned back. I don't know, of course.

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: The last name I circled, "Marko Fumic," he and his family were forced to exchange properties. On one occasion, a group that I didn't know came to see him in order to kill him, to eliminate him. That was a group from the Slavonija region, at the time when Serbian Krajina was in existence, or immediately prior to that; and that was the reason why Marko Fumic had to leave, had to exchange the property. And later on, shortly thereafter, his brother did something similar. Milan didn't have similar problems, that is to say, did not have threats, except for this atmosphere of fear and the need to follow his brother, because that's what their mother advised them to do, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: So all these Fumic -- all these members of the Fumic family that is from the list, number 205, 6, 7, 8, 9 and 10, were forced to leave?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: I only mentioned Marko Fumic and his family. As for the atmosphere of fear, that was a sort of a coercion against his brother. Since Milan Fumic at that time had refugees staying in his house whom he supported. And despite of that, he left.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: So could you circle also "Fumic, Milan," or not? "Fumic, Milan," is number 210.

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: I could circle "Milan Fumic" in the sense that he was an official member of the local commune board. He told me that many times. We see each other nowadays frequently. He comes to Hrtkovci and I go to see him. And he told me at the meetings of the local commune at the time, Rade Cakmak, who became a member of the board, and Fumic and some other people were part of the previous membership when there were 15 of them; so Cakmak would always threaten him and would always make comments to the effect that he couldn't sit next to an Ustasha at a meeting, referring to Milan Fumic as an Ustasha. This is what caused Milan Fumic to be afraid and to decide to follow his brother.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Don't hurry in reading the names. You're here for this reason. I understand it's a boring task, but ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, I just want to be sure I understand fully the purpose why we're going through this list. I suppose that at some point we will have the author of the list produced as an expert witness in this court, and at that point she can testify to the accuracy of the list. So what is it now that you want to elicit from this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: That the witness personally witnessed -- sorry, the people who were forced to leave. The expert, of course, got this data after, but he was there when these people were forced to leave and he can tell us something about these people. The expert, I think, cannot say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: So the purpose of confronting this witness with the list is for this witness to explain to us the reasons why these people left?

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: The people that he knew among these ones. Of course, he didn't know all these 800 people, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I understand. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Ferrara, to gain time, since there is a great number of pages, wouldn't it be better --

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: If the Chamber agrees --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- for him to read the list this afternoon?

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Absolutely. I will continue tomorrow this part of the examination-in-chief. So let's move to another topic for the last 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment, please. I'd like to put a question to my fellow Judges.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, we are going to finish in ten minutes' time. You'll take the document with you, and this could entertain you this afternoon. You can draw circles around the names you know and bring this document back tomorrow morning. After having looked at all these pages and names, you will be able to tell us which people left. Otherwise, we're going to spend a lot of time on this. So you shall take the documents away with you and draw your circles in the course of the afternoon or this evening, and bring the document back tomorrow morning. Please proceed, Mr. Ferrara.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Mr. Ejic, was -- you say -- I think you already said it. Was the local and international press interested in what was happening in Hrtkovci?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: Yes, they were interested.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: We are in closed session?

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Were you interviewed at the time by some journalist?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was, by many journalists, local ones and foreign ones. I can't remember all of their names, but some of the foreign media organisations I remember. I gave a statement to Zidovec [phoen] at "Zeitung." I gave statements to some Slovenian newspapers, to Globus, to Croatian papers. I also held a press conference in Belgrade, where I gave a statement both for local and foreign journalists. And then there were also cases where press conferences were held in Hrtkovci and where I gave statements for the press. I and many other people did.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection. I suppose that the witness said that to the OTP when they interviewed him first, and the OTP was duty-bound to obtain the text of all of these interviews that the witness had given to journalists, and the OTP should have disclosed this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, you told the investigators that you gave interviews, and did you give a list of all these interviews?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that I mentioned that I gave statements. Now, as to whether I actually gave them the names of media organisations --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Was the investigator interested in this? Did he just listen to you and move on or did he ask you on what date such-and-such an article had been published? Did you just say this and then he moved on to something else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I only mentioned it. They didn't ask me for details.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At what time did you give these interviews?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I gave interviews after the rally. I think that I gave before as well, but most interviews I gave after the rally and after the exchanges stepped up.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: I want to show you one of these interviews. This is 65 ter number 1544, disclosed to the accused on 14 September 2007, and received number 71. Can we have it on the screen?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, there are at least one of these that has been disclosed to you, this one.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is, but I think that all of them should have been disclosed, because this is not the text of an interview. This is a text of the journalist who wrote about the Hrtkovci affair. This is not the text of an interview.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's true. This is an article which was written --

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Your Honours, the interview is inside the article, of course. It's a part of the article is the interview with the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We'll have a look at this. Please proceed. We shall, in any event, come across the name of the school teacher I mentioned; Zelica Tkalac.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Mr. Ejic, do you remember this interview with this journalist of the "St. Petersburg Times," I think is the newspaper?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSA EJIC
utterances.text: I remember giving one such interview.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Once again I have to observe that this is not an interview. There is one single sentence that the author quotes and that was allegedly uttered by this witness, one single sentence on page 4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, if we are talking about something specifically journalistic, this is not an interview, per se, this is a press article. Even if one sentence is quoted, this is a press article.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We agree. We agree so much, sir, that we need to stop now because it is a quarter past 1.00. The Registrar will give me the time calculation. The instructions for the witness is to draw the circle through the names he knows and not to contact or speak to anyone. And we shall resume our hearing tomorrow morning. A slight change, however. Instead of starting at 8.30, we shall start at 9.00, because I am not sitting in any case in the afternoon, so we can start at 9.00 tomorrow morning. The hearing would start at 9.00 for tomorrow morning, therefore, and will run on until a quarter to 2.00. We shall proceed in the same manner on Thursday. I wish you all a very pleasant afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
